minus.text: Osroene and Nisibis, Sasanian from 252 to Odaenathus's recapture in spring 262 (sasanian-empire_261, palmyrene-empire ledger/3)

region.text: Anatolia as the Roman Empire held it in 259, without Osroene and Nisibis: the 'Asia' of the East taken by Macrianus and Quietus, which Gallienus's side recovers in 261 (Syria, Phoenice and Palaestina go to Odaenathus by the palmyrene-empire_261 keyframe, Egypt to Rome in 262 by events/1)

events.note: 261: the usurpation of Macrianus and Quietus collapses. 'Both Macrianus were eventually defeated at Illyricum by Aureolus' and Quietus was 'sieged by Odaenathus in Emesa with Ballista and killed'; the East, which 'Chaos consumed ... following the capture of Valerian', 'was eventually pacified by Odaenathus', whom Gallienus named Dux Romanorum. The draft dissolves the usurpers into nobody's land (4,143 cells of Anatolia, Syria and Egypt grey from 261 to 270) because no dossier gains them back; Anatolia returns to the Roman Empire here, and Egypt in 262 (events/1). Syria, Lebanon and Israel are left out of this gain so that the palmyrene-empire_261 keyframe (Syria, Phoenice and Palaestina, 'held after the defeat of Quietus and Macrianus at Emesa in 261') takes them from the usurpers as in the dossier; Osroene with Nisibis is left out too, being Persian until Odaenathus's recapture of spring 262 (it is nobody's in 261, as in the draft, and Palmyrene from 262). The first version of this event included both and so drew Syria, Phoenice, Palaestina and Osroene as Roman in 261 (reviewer's correction).

region.text: Egypt as the Roman Empire held it in 259: Aemilianus's Egypt, 'c. 261 - 262 (Egypt)', defeated by Aurelius Theodotus

events.note: 262: Egypt returns to Gallienus. The usurper Aemilianus held Egypt 'c. 261 - 262 (Egypt)' and was 'Defeated by Aurelius Theodotus'; with him gone Egypt is Roman again until Zenobia takes it in October-November 270 (palmyrene-empire ledger/8). Without this the draft leaves Egypt grey until the roman-empire_270 keyframe.

region.text: the Albanian kingdom (the 259 outline without the right bank), which 'acknowledged the suzerainty of the Sasanian Empire' in 252

events.note: 252: 'In 252, Caucasian Albania acknowledged the suzerainty of the Sasanian Empire'; 'Albania became a vassal state of the Sassanid Empire' but 'retained its monarchy'. Roman protectorate again from 297 ('the treaty of Nisibis stipulated the reestablishment of the Roman protectorate over Caucasian Iberia and Albania'). The draft instead gives all 180 cells to the Sasanian Empire from 260 (rule R2: caucasian-albania lists the Sasanian Empire as its successor in 510) and leaves the kingdom landless to 299.

region.text: Anatolia as the Roman Empire held it in 259: the cells the Palmyrene keyframe of 270 drops (Cilicia, Cappadocia, Galatia) and nobody holds until Aurelian's campaign of 272

events.note: 271: Anatolia is still Rome's (the cells are nobody's from 270, when a keyframe snap, applied after the year's events, drops them). 'In 271, Zabbai started the operations in Asia Minor' and 'The Palmyrenes subdued Galatia, and occupied Ancyra' (the Palmyrene dossier takes Galatia from Rome in 271, ledger/9); 'In 272, Aurelian crossed the Bosphorus and advanced quickly through Anatolia'. The palmyrene-empire_270 keyframe holds only Syria, Phoenice, Palaestina, Osroene, Arabia and Egypt, so once Rome's 267 loss (ledger/96, 'large parts of Asia Minor') is drawn, the 645 Anatolian cells that keyframe drops go to nobody and stay grey to 283 (about 480 cells in 272-282). They return to Rome here.

minus.text: the Murong home ground in the Daling basin round Jicheng (Jinzhou) and Chaoyang, less the Yuwen disc round Chifeng

region.text: the steppe of Cliopatria's Xianbei shape of 224 (Inner Mongolia and the Great Wall strip) outside the Murong home ground in the Daling basin

events.note: 236: the Murong keep only Liaoxi. Kebineng was 'assassinated by a Cao Wei agent in 235, after which his confederacy disintegrated'; 'The Murong settled in Liaodong' and helped Wei against the Gongsun in 238, the Duan and Yuwen settled in Liaoxi and the Tuoba only near Shengle/Hohhot in 258 ('The article does not show' any Xianbei state on the steppe). The draft passes the whole dissolved Xianbei land (2,265 cells of Inner Mongolia and Shanxi, drawn as a Wei vassal) to the Murong at the end of 235 (xianbei successor placeholder) although the Murong dossier's own keyframe for 235-284 is the Daling basin (about 130 cells); the surplus is released to nobody until the Tuoba, Duan and Yuwen dossiers exist (year 236 because a dissolve is applied at the end of its year).

region.text: Sakastan (Sistan): Iranian Sistan and the Zaranj country of Nimroz

events.note: ca. 240: Sakastan is a Sasanian province. 'The province was formed in ca. 240, during the reign of Shapur I'; its ruler 'Ardashir Sakanshah became a Sasanian vassal during the reign of Shapur's father Ardashir I (r. 224-242)'; Shapur's son Narseh governed it to 271, Hormizd after him, and Bahram II put down his revolt in 283. The sasanian-empire_238 keyframe (Cliopatria) leaves the Afghan part (133 cells of Nimroz) out until the 283 keyframe, so the cells fall to nobody from 238 to 282; they are Sasanian here from 240.

union.text: Guizhou without the 21 cells of its south-eastern corner (Liping, Congjiang) that Cliopatria's Eastern Wu shape of 238-270 holds and Wu holds in the draft from 224 to 280

correction.text: Cliopatria's Shu Han shape of 224 (Yi Province's western lands and Hanzhong) plus the Chongqing Three Gorges cells and the whole of Nanzhong, Yunnan with Yongchang and Guizhou: 'based in the area around present-day Hanzhong, Sichuan, Chongqing, Yunnan, Guizhou, and north Guangxi'

keyframe_overrides.why: Cliopatria's Shu Han shape stops at 100.9 E and so omits Yongchang in west Yunnan; the page puts the state 'around present-day Hanzhong, Sichuan, Chongqing, Yunnan, Guizhou, and north Guangxi' and says Zhuge Liang 'launched an expeditionary force there in 225 to quell local rebellions'. Starts in 225 (the year of the Nanzhong campaign; 224 stays with shu-han_219, as the dossier note says) and adds the rest of Yunnan and Guizhou so that the 225 gain (ledger/15) and the later keyframes agree. Replaces the draft's 224 snap (+1,739 cells) and 225 gain (+917), which left Shu 1,500 cells too large in 225-237 and then cut 1,498 cells at the 238 snap. Reviewer's correction: the south-eastern corner of Guizhou that Cliopatria draws as Eastern Wu's (21 cells, Wu's in the draft 224-280) is left out; with it, Shu took the corner from Wu at the 238 snap and it fell to nobody at Shu's end in 263.
